    {
      "startEvent": 980,
      "endEvent": 984,
      "contextStartEvent": 970,
      "contextEndEvent": 1016,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "the universe is everything that is ever was or ever shall be",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The formula establishes that God must belong to the universe and therefore need a cause (E981–984), without separately earning that causal inference. However, E985–1016 develop an ordinary regress objection and acknowledge ignorance. This may be a disputed definition within an argument rather than an affirmation replacing argument."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1051,
      "endEvent": 1055,
      "contextStartEvent": 1023,
      "contextEndEvent": 1060,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "you can know the truth and the truth shall make you free",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["comfort"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The affirmation helps dismiss probabilistic confidence in favor of certainty. E1025–1031 supply examples and a self-reference objection, but neither explains why knowing truths invalidates degrees of confidence; the freedom promise supplies no bridge. The surrounding argument matters, and rejecting Cromwell's rule does not itself immunize every belief against criticism."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1255,
      "endEvent": 1257,
      "contextStartEvent": 1235,
      "contextEndEvent": 1265,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "Jesus's people conquered the world by loving their enemies",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "yes",
      "protection": "no",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "This compact historical verdict supplies Christianity's favorable contrast with Islam without evidence that enemy-love caused its worldwide expansion. E1249–1254 give a teaching and explicitly restrict compliant followers; those support a prescribed ethic, not the claimed historical result. The invitation to compare documents at E1241–1245 remains open to evidence."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2065,
      "endEvent": 2075,
      "contextStartEvent": 2037,
      "contextEndEvent": 2088,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "all the arguments against Jesus and the resurrection are based on a prior commitment to naturalism",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The blanket attribution risks disqualifying resurrection objections by their alleged assumptions before considering their merits. But E2067–2069 audibly qualify the universal claim, and E2075–2088 explicitly permit disproof. The passage could target circular objections specifically rather than exclude all contrary historical evidence; protective use therefore remains uncertain."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2115,
      "endEvent": 2129,
      "contextStartEvent": 2097,
      "contextEndEvent": 2157,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "you don't always know why I do things",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "no",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["comfort"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Unknown divine reasons, trust, and salvation after suffering answer the general challenge without limiting which suffering they can reconcile with divine love (E2115–2129). This protects against contrary suffering patterns through unseen purposes and compensation. Butt acknowledges the time limit and incomplete answer at E2102–2108; the response is an argument, not a slogan."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2524,
      "endEvent": 2535,
      "contextStartEvent": 2488,
      "contextEndEvent": 2536,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "a loving God who can make everything right in the end",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["comfort"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Unlimited eventual restoration could render the friend's lasting paralysis irrelevant to divine goodness. Yet E2531–2535 explicitly condition the response on an afterlife, and E2524–2528 describe other people's reactions rather than establish God's existence from them. The passage may offer conditional consolation rather than substitute proof or conclusively neutralize the objection."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 2695,
      "endEvent": 2699,
      "contextStartEvent": 2676,
      "contextEndEvent": 2792,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "there's no such thing as the supernatural or the Paranormal",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "yes",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "The categorical formula exceeds the historical witchcraft example, although E2722–2732 allow supernatural possibilities. More decisively, E2742–2746 promise acceptance if measurable and immediately declare measurement impossible by definition, closing that test. Subsequent mechanism questions and the amputee comparison supply substantive reasons, making substitution uncertain despite the explicit protective condition."
    }
  ],
  "contrasts": [
    {
      "startEvent": 2577,
      "endEvent": 2589,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "we shouldn't take anything as absolute truth just because there's a consensus",
      "explanation": "Shermer explicitly allows consensus to be wrong and treats competing researchers' scrutiny as increasing provisional confidence. E2554–2569 explain the corrective process and its limits, so the compact conclusion summarizes supplied reasons."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1157,
      "endEvent": 1169,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "just because you don't know everything doesn't mean you don't know something",
      "explanation": "Butt distinguishes complete knowledge from knowledge of particular claims, then identifies the attributes he thinks his earlier causation, design, and morality arguments establish. Those arguments remain disputable, but the catchphrase articulates a relevant distinction rather than replacing them."
    }
